To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Adaptive Ridge regression and its extension, the Adaptive Ridge with Consistent Signs (ARCOS) regression, are the best methods for network inference from steady state data.
the Adaptive Ridge ( AR) regression and the new extension thereof, the Consistent AR regression, outperform other methods for the reconstruction of gene regulatory networks from qPCR data.

the Adaptive Ridge regression is the best method for reconstructing gene networks from time series data, and that adding constraints reflecting biological circuit design can further improve the reconstruction performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new methods for network inference from time series data, and with applying them to real data sets.
the development and testing of methods for inferring biomolecular regulatory networks.
the reconstruction of biomolecular regulatory networks from time series data using linear regression models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of biological constraints and penalized regression is a powerful and flexible method for network inference.
the AR algorithm, which is an adaptive L2 penalized regression, is the most robust and accurate algorithm tested.
AR is the best method in terms of accuracy, while L1 is the best method for sparseness and the new method is the best for both.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed an algorithm that combines the best of both worlds, namely the biological constraints and the statistical inference.

we developed an inference method for linear regulatory networks that is able to reconstruct networks with a high accuracy and that we extended this method to include biologically motivated constraints.
the AR regression method with the new constraint is a very powerful tool for the reconstruction of transcriptional regulatory network from gene expression data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of biological knowledge with penalized regression methods is a powerful tool in the quest for the reconstruction of regulatory networks from high-throughput time series measurements.
the combination of a biologically motivated constraint and the AR regression leads to the best reconstruction of a network from time series data.
combining biological knowledge with statistical methods can significantly improve the reconstruction of regulatory networks.
